title: Release + Launch Security Checklist and Signoff (RBAC v2 / SIEM / Audit)
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures the minimal security checks and signoff artifacts we require for product releases and launches that touch authentication, authorization (RBAC v2), audit logging, and SIEM exports. It is intended to be a practical, checklist-first doc that release owners can follow and attach to release tickets.

Scope / When to use:
- Any release that: modifies RBAC (roles, role-mappings, inheritance), changes audit log schema, adds or alters SIEM export pipeline, or modifies evidence-generation automation.
- Applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment rollouts.
- Not intended for purely UI copy changes unless they touch auth/telemetry.

Quick decision matrix (high-level):
- RBAC code change? -> Full RBAC v2 validation (see section).
- Audit fields added/removed? -> Schema diff + sample events to SIEM staging.
- SIEM export format changes? -> End-to-end test w/ SIEM staging + RU/ops signoff.
- Evidence automation changes? -> Unit test + smoke pipeline run + artifact store verification.

RBAC v2 Validation (required steps):
1) Change summary: include short bullet summary of RBAC changes in release ticket (roles added, changed permissions, resources affected).
2) Unit tests: all role/permission checks must have automated coverage. Attach test run URL or CI job id.
3) Staging smoke tests: run the RBAC smoke script (scripts/rbac/test_smoke_v2.sh) against staging. Expected output: no 403s for allowed flows; explicit denial for disallowed flows. Paste a 20-line excerpt of the smoke run into the release ticket.
4) Principle of least privilege review: product owner and security engineer must sign off on any role that is broader than existing equivalents. If widening scope, fill the exception form below.
5) Backwards compatibility: ensure role IDs and audit-affected resource identifiers remain stable where documented. If breaking, note migration steps.

Audit Log Schema Validation:
- Goal: guarantee downstream consumers (SIEM, retention, compliance reports) continue to parse events.
- Steps:
  a) Generate a schema diff (we have a script: tools/audit/schema-diff.py). Attach diff output.
  b) Produce representative sample events (min 3 per changed event type) and upload to /evidence/audit-samples/<release-id> in S3. Filenames should include event_type + timestamp.
  c) Validate timestamp formats (ISO8601 with timezone), principal_id presence, and event_id uniqueness. The CI will fail on missing fields; attach the CI job link.
- Example (sample event) copied into ticket: 
  {"timestamp":"2026-02-27T14:12:02Z","event_type":"policy.update","principal_id":"user:maya","resource":"arn:ri:project:123","changes":[{"field":"bindings","from":"read","to":"write"}],"audit_id":"AUD-20260227-7c8f"}

SIEM Export / Mapping Checks:
- End-to-end test required for any change to export pipeline or schema. Steps:
  1) Deploy to SIEM staging connector.
  2) Send a curated mini-batch (use tools/siem/send-test-batch.sh) and confirm events arrive and parse in staging dashboards. Attach screenshots of parsed fields.
  3) Validate field mappings: ensure host, service, principal_id, event_type, timestamp, audit_id, and severity map to expected SIEM fields. If a field is new/renamed, update SIEM mapping doc (confluence:siem/mappings) and include mapping diff.
  4) Retention/PII check: confirm that any PII fields are redacted or routed to restricted index; note index name.

Evidence Automation (how we gather signoff artifacts):
- Artifact sources we expect to be present on successful checklist:
  * CI job URL for RBAC test suite (e.g., https://ci.redwood/1234)
  * S3 evidence folder: s3://redwood-evidence/releases/<release-id>/ (must contain audit-samples/, siem-screens/, rbac-smoke.txt)
  * Automated screenshots/logs for SIEM staging parsing (append timestamped filenames)
- Commands to generate artifacts (team can re-run before signoff):
  * python tools/audit/schema-diff.py --base main --head ${PR} > /tmp/schema-diff.txt
  * ./tools/rbac/generate-smoke.sh --output /tmp/rbac-smoke.txt && aws s3 cp /tmp/rbac-smoke.txt s3://redwood-evidence/releases/${RELEASE_ID}/rbac-smoke.txt
  * ./tools/siem/send-test-batch.sh --file /tmp/siem-batch.json && aws s3 cp siem-screens/*.png s3://redwood-evidence/releases/${RELEASE_ID}/siem-screens/
- Evidence automation checks in CI: the release job should include a step that verifies presence of required files in the S3 path. If missing, gate fails.

Signoff template (to paste into release ticket):
- Release id: <RELEASE_ID>
- RBAC change summary: <one-line>
- Audit diff attached: <s3 path or CI job>
- SIEM staging run: <link/screenshots>
- Evidence S3 path: s3://redwood-evidence/releases/<RELEASE_ID>/
- Approvers (must include at least 2):
  * Product owner: <name> (signature/ok)
  * Security engineer: <name> (signature/ok)
  * Infra/ops: <name> (signature/ok)
- Final status: approved | exception_granted | blocked

Exception approval flow (if checks fail or a deliberate deviation is requested):
1) Create an exception request ticket (label: security-exception) with: affected change, business justification, proposed mitigation (timeboxed), and compensating controls.
2) Required reviewers for exception: security lead, product owner, infra lead. Include a rollback plan.
3) Minimum exception metadata: duration (max 90 days), risk level (low/med/high), monitoring hooks (alerts), and evidence of compensating controls (e.g., additional logging, alert rules).
4) Exception template snippet to include in ticket: 
  - exception_id: EXC-<auto>
  - scope: "RBAC: role X widened to Y"
  - justification: "needed for rollout because ..."
  - compensations: "added alert on policy.change to PagerDuty, daily digest to security@redwood.com"
  - expiry: YYYY-MM-DD
4) Security lead closes exception by marking status=granted or rejected; if granted, gate allowed but require a follow-up audit before expiry.

Release checklist (copy these into the release ticket as checkboxes):
- [ ] RBAC change summary added to ticket
- [ ] Unit tests attached (links)
- [ ] RBAC smoke run uploaded to evidence bucket
- [ ] Schema diff for audit logs attached
- [ ] Sample events uploaded (>=3 per changed event type)
- [ ] SIEM staging run completed + screenshots attached
- [ ] PII/redaction statement included if PII present
- [ ] Approvers listed and at least 2 have signed off
- [ ] Evidence S3 path present and contains expected files
- [ ] Exception request created if any step failed/was skipped

Operational notes / gotchas (learned from past releases):
- When renaming event_type strings, remember to update both consumers and retention queries; silent failures observed when only one side updated.
- RBAC v2 role_id renames are especially disruptive to Dedicated deployments where cached role policy blobs can persist; include a cache flush job in rollout steps.
- SIEM mappings occasionally drop fields if the connector schema is too strict; prefer additive changes with null-safe mapping.
- If an exception is approved, add a monitoring dashboard widget specific to the exception window.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Auto-detect breaking audit schema diffs and post a bot comment on the PR with impacted consumers (SEC-423 is driving this work).
- Add a standard retention index naming convention for releases to reduce cross-team confusion.

Owners / contacts:
